{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793057936488,"sessionID":"ses_e856cd463ffeC6rs1MWpP0j724","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01BAcczoJdTwebqmLF9iu7nM","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <omp.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Visit every cell of the row (y, z) and pass its Laplacian to op(x, lap).\n// The Laplacian uses clamped boundary conditions. Expression order matches the\n// original per-cell formulation so results are bit-identical.\n// Rows are addressed through raw pointers so the inner loop optimizes well\n// inside OpenMP-outlined regions.\ntemplate <typename Op>\ninline void forEachCellLaplacian(const double* c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                 const double ddx, const double ddy, const double ddz,\n                                 const size_t y, const size_t z, Op&& op) {\n    const size_t nxy = nx * ny;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n\n    const double* rowC  = c + z * nxy + y * nx;\n    const double* rowYp = c + z * nxy + yp * nx;\n    const double* rowYn = c + z * nxy + yn * nx;\n    const double* rowZp = c + zp * nxy + y * nx;\n    const double* rowZn = c + zn * nxy + y * nx;\n\n    for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n        const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n        const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n        const double center = rowC[x];\n\n        const double cxx = (rowC[xp] + rowC[xn] - 2.0 * center) / ddx;\n        const double cyy = (rowYp[x] + rowYn[x] - 2.0 * center) / ddy;\n        const double czz = (rowZp[x] + rowZn[x] - 2.0 * center) / ddz;\n\n        op(x, cxx + cyy + czz);\n    }\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential\nvoid computeChemicalPotential(const std::vector<double>& c, std::vector<double>& mu,\n                              const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                              const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                              const double gamma, const double e_AA, const double e_BB, const double e_AB) {\n    const double* __restrict cp = c.data();\n    double* __restrict mup = mu.data();\n    const double ddx = dx * dx;\n    const double ddy = dy * dy;\n    const double ddz = dz * dz;\n\n    // Each (z, y) row writes only its own cells of mu; The expression order matches\n// the original per-cell formulation so results are bit-identical.\n// Rows are addressed through raw pointers so the inner loop optimizes well\n// inside OpenMP-outlined }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update step\nvoid cahnHilliardUpdate(std::vector<double>& cnew, const std::vector<double>& cold,\n                        const std::vector<double>& mu,\n printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n\n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    printf(\"OpenMP threads: %d\\n\", omp_get_max_threads());\n\n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n\n    size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n\n    // Allocate arrays\n    std::vector<double> cold(gridSize);\n    std::vector<double> cnew(gridSize);\n    std::vector<double> mu(gridSize);\n\n    // Initialize concentration field\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n    initializeConcentration(cold, nx, ny, {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793058050263,"sessionID":"ses_e856cd463ffeC6rs1MWpP0j724","part":{"id":"prt_17a9665a4001M6yRXOWFX2RJMe","messageID":"msg_17a966229001HRO7a2RgkRgqsF","sessionID":"ses_e856cd463ffeC6rs1MWpP0j724","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing the divisions remain the real cost here—three vdivsd per cell in both the mu calculation and update step—and I'm wondering if the original O3 build got specialized in a way that avoided this overhead.\n\nMy theory: if computeChemicalPotential got inlined into main with dx=1.0 as a known constant, then x/1.0 would fold away trivially. The OpenMP-outlined version, by contrast, receives ddx through a captured struct, blocking that constant propagation entirely. The fix needs to preserve general semantics for arbitrary dx while still recovering this fold when dx happens to equal 1.0.\n\nSince dx=1.0 is exact in this case, I could add a runtime check that detects when grid spacings all equal 1.0 and skips the divisions entirely as an identity operation, falling back to the general division path otherwise — this preserves exact semantics while avoiding the division cost in the common case.\n\nThe other minor division operations in initializeConcentration are negligible overhead, and the memset-style initialization looks fine as-is.\n\nNow I'm adding a compile-time template flag to the Laplacian computation that skips the division entirely when spacing is uniform (1.0), verifying that dividing by 1.0 is bit-identical to the raw value even for edge cases like negative zero.\n\nWriting templated kernels...\n\nThe pragma should work fine inside a template function, and the dispatch just checks if spacing is unit before choosing the templated path at compile time. I'll go ahead and make the edits to the file now.\n\n","time":{"start":1793058039204,"end":1793058050224},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793058050263,"sessionID":"ses_e856cd463ffeC6rs1MWpP0j724","part":{"id":"prt_17a9690b3001hk0wVtnGN9QlME","messageID":"msg_17a966229001HRO7a2RgkRgqsF","sessionID":"ses_e856cd463ffeC6rs1MWpP0j724","type":"text","text":"The profile shows the cause. Each cell still performs three `vdivsd` for the Laplacian, because the spacing is a runtime value inside the OpenMP-outlined body. The original's divisions were folded to constants after inlining. Division by exactly 1.0 is an exact identity in IEEE arithmetic, so I'll add a compile-time `UnitSpacing` path that skips the division only when dx, dy, and dz all equal 1.0. The general path keeps the division for other spacings.","time":{"start":1793058050227,"end":1793058050241}}}

But scaling looks off — 16 threads gives 79ms while 64 threads balloons to 196ms, which seems backwards. I suspect noisy measurements from a shared machine or other tenants affecting CPU availability, rather than a real algorithmic issue.\n\nActually, thinking more about the hardware topology — 128 physical cores, 256 threads with hyperthreading across two sockets — this looks like a NUMA problem. The main thread's serial initialization of the vectors first-touches all the memory pages on one NUMA node, so once we scale past one socket's worth of cores, we're bottlenecked by remote memory access and limited bandwidth to a single node. The array sizes here are large enough to be genuinely memory-bound, so this fits. The fix would be to parallelize the initial array fill with the same scheduling as the main computation so pages get distributed across both NUMA nodes, though I need to be careful not to break the vector type used elsewhere for output.\n\n","time":{"start":1793058085707,"end":1793058092422},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
